title: Crispy Panko Haddock with Lemon Rice
subtitle: flaky haddock under a golden buttery panko crust, with lemony rice, peas and a quick tartar sauce
imageAlt: Golden panko-crusted haddock fillets on lemon rice with peas and a small dish of tartar sauce on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: dinner for one big eater + one hungry eater, plus 2 lunches

beforeYouStart.text: Thaw frozen haddock in the fridge overnight, or sealed in cold water 30–45 minutes, and pat it very dry.
Start the rice first; the fish bakes in 12–15 minutes.

steps.title: Start the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring it to a boil with the water and a pinch of salt, cover and simmer on low 15 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat with the lid on. Fluff with a fork.

steps.title: Prep the fish
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and line a baking sheet with parchment. Pat the haddock very dry, season with the salt and pepper and spread the tops thinly with the 2 tbsp mayonnaise.

steps.title: Crust
steps.text: Mix the panko, melted butter, garlic powder and paprika and press it firmly onto the tops of the fish.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake 12–15 minutes, until the crust is golden and the fish flakes easily and reads 70°C (158°F) in the thickest part.

steps.title: Tartar sauce
steps.text: Zest and juice 1 lemon and cut the other in wedges. Stir the ⅓ cup mayonnaise, pickles and 1 tsp lemon juice together.

steps.title: Lemon rice
steps.text: Microwave the peas covered with a splash of water 3 minutes. Fold them into the hot rice with the butter, lemon zest and 1 tbsp lemon juice.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve the haddock on the rice with the tartar sauce and lemon wedges.

fixIt.fix: It wasn't dried well after thawing. Pat it very dry and use a hot oven.
Broil 1–2 minutes at the end, watching closely.
Lift it with a wide spatula; haddock is delicate when cooked.

saleTip: Frozen haddock and cod fillets drop to about $8.99 for 454 g on sale at No Frills.
swap: Cod or pollock: same timing. Store-bought tartar sauce works too.
leftovers: Flake leftover fish into fish cakes or tacos.
doneness: Fish at 70°C (158°F): opaque and flakes easily (Health Canada, fish).
source: Based on tested panko-crusted baked fish methods (Canadian Living, Hellmann's Canada): a thin mayonnaise layer under buttered panko, baked at 220°C; a simple pickle tartar sauce.
prepAhead: Make the tartar sauce up to 4 days ahead.
Mix the crumb topping up to 3 days ahead.
reheat: Fish on a rack at 200°C (400°F) for 8 minutes, until 74°C (165°F); rice in the microwave with a splash of water.

basic.note: Panko haddock with plain buttered rice and peas; no tartar or paprika.

fancy.note: Parmesan in the crust and a lemon butter drizzle.

stepNotes.2: Fancy: mix the Parmesan into the crumbs.

addSteps.title: Lemon butter
addSteps.text: Melt the butter with 1 tbsp lemon juice and spoon it over the fish at the table.

plating: Fish leaning on a mound of rice.
Tartar sauce in a little dish.

why.0-3: Mayonnaise keeps the fish moist and holds the crumbs in place.
why.0-4: Panko stays crisp in the oven where regular crumbs go soft.
why.2-1: Sweet pickles give the tartar sauce its tang.

funFact: Haddock is the traditional fish for fish and chips in Atlantic Canada and Scotland; cod is more common in England.

keeps.note: cooked fish loses its crunch when frozen

airFryer: Air-fry the crusted haddock crumb side up at 200°C (400°F) for 8–10 minutes, until golden and the fish flakes and reads 70°C (158°F). Line the basket with perforated parchment so it lifts out in one piece.
